title: Texas-Style Chocolate Sheet Cake with Pecan Icing
changes_from_base: Creamed yellow cake replaced by a hot-mixed cocoa cake; warm cocoa icing poured over the hot cake with toasted pecans.
summary: This uses the same tin, oven and portions as the classic yellow sheet cake, but the creamed batter is replaced by a hot-mixed cocoa cake, iced while still hot with a warm cocoa icing and toasted pecans. Thin, moist and ideal for feeding a crowd.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm metal baking tin (not glass), greased

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Heat oven, toast pecans
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes with a shelf in the middle. Toast the pecans on the small baking tray for 6-8 minutes until fragrant, then set aside. Toasting deepens their nutty flavour and keeps them crunchy under the icing.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, caster sugar, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in the large bowl and make a well in the centre.

steps.title: Bloom the cocoa
steps.text: Melt the 170 g butter in the saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the cocoa, then the just-boiled water, and let it bubble for 30 seconds. Hot liquid dissolves the cocoa and releases its flavour compounds, giving a deeper, rounder chocolate taste.

steps.title: Combine the batter
steps.text: Pour the chocolate mixture into the well and fold just until no flour shows, keeping the pan aside for the icing. Whisk the soured cream, eggs and vanilla together, then fold them into the batter until even. The soured cream reacts with the bicarbonate to lift the cake and keeps the crumb moist.

steps.title: Bake the cake
steps.text: Pour the batter into the greased metal tin and spread it right into the corners. Bake for 22-28 minutes until a skewer in the centre comes out with a few moist crumbs. A metal tin conducts heat quickly and evenly, so the thin layer bakes through without drying at the edges, which a glass dish can cause.

steps.title: Make the icing
steps.text: During the last 5 minutes of baking, melt the 115 g butter in the same pan and whisk in the cocoa until bubbling. Off the heat, whisk in the milk, vanilla and icing sugar until smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Ice while hot
steps.text: As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, pour the warm icing over it and spread quickly, then scatter over the pecans. The icing sets as it cools, sealing in moisture and forming a thin, fudgy layer on top.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.text: Cool on the wire rack for 1 hour, then chill for 30 minutes if you want clean squares. Cut into 15 pieces.

tips: A common mistake is letting the icing cool before pouring; it thickens fast, so time it for the last minutes of baking and pour straight onto the hot cake.
Use natural cocoa powder, as its acidity reacts with the bicarbonate of soda to make the cake rise.
Wipe the knife between cuts for neat squares.
Avoid overbaking: a few moist crumbs on the skewer mean the cake will stay tender once iced.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store covered at room temperature for up to 3 days. Squares freeze well, wrapped, for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature.
